issue.title: Settle a sudo gate from a preserved on-disk ledger without rerunning commands
issue.description:
## Feature proposal

After a detached sudo runner has written a valid `ledger.json`, Bryan should be able to settle the gate from that preserved ledger without re-running the selected commands. Today `sase sudo answer --run` always re-executes, and a failed finalize leaves the gate pending even when the on-disk ledger is complete.

This is outside the large-ledger settlement work: that change only trims oversized tails so a completed ledger can pass the 64 KiB approve-input bound, and it publishes a finalize-failure notification. Rerun-on-reapproval semantics were an explicit non-goal of `plan:202610/sudo_large_ledger_settlement.md`.

task_type_fields.proposal: After ledger.json exists, sase sudo answer and finalize should be able to settle from that preserved ledger without re-executing the selected commands.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: plan:202610/sudo_large_ledger_settlement.md only fits oversized tails and notifies on finalize failure; rerun-on-reapproval semantics were an explicit non-goal.

issue.creation_reason: After a detached runner writes a valid ledger, re-approval currently reruns the selected commands. The large-ledger settlement plan left this recovery path as an explicit follow-up.
